title: Large Language Models Reproduce Racial Stereotypes When Used for Text Annotation
abstract: arXiv:2603.13891v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for automated text annotation in tasks ranging from academic research to content moderation and hiring. Across 19 LLMs and two experiments totaling more than 4 million annotation judgments, we show that subtle identity cues embedded in text systematically bias annotation outcomes in ways that mirror racial stereotypes. In a names-based experiment spanning 39 annotation tasks, texts containing names associated with Black individuals are rated as more aggressive by 18 of 19 models and more gossipy by 18 of 19. Asian names produce a bamboo-ceiling profile: 17 of 19 models rate individuals as more intelligent, while 18 of 19 rate them as less confident and less sociable. Arab names elicit cognitive elevation alongside interpersonal devaluation, and all four minority groups are consistently rated as less self-disciplined. translated_title: 大型语言模型在文本标注中复现种族刻板印象
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于自动化文本标注，任务范围从学术研究到内容审核和招聘。通过19个LLMs和两项实验，总计超过400万条标注判断，我们表明文本中嵌入的微妙身份线索系统地偏置了标注结果，其方式反映了种族刻板印象。在一项基于名字的实验（涵盖39个标注任务）中，包含与黑人个体相关名字的文本被19个模型中的18个评为更具攻击性，被19个中的18个评为更八卦。亚洲名字产生了“竹子天花板”特征：19个模型中的17个将个体评为更聪明，而19个中的18个将其评为更不自信和更不善于社交。阿拉伯名字引发认知提升和人际贬低并存，所有四个少数群体始终被评为自律性较低。在一项匹配方言实验中，同一句子被判断为……
tldr: 本研究发现大型语言模型在文本标注中系统性复现种族刻板印象，基于名字或方言的微妙线索会显著偏置模型对文本的评判结果。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that large language models systematically reproduce racial stereotypes in text annotation, where subtle cues from names or dialects significantly bias model judgments.
